doc.citation: Molyneux, S. G., Barron, H. F. & Smith, R. A. 2008. Upper Llandovery–Wenlock (Silurian) palynology of the Pentland Hills inliers, Midland Valley of Scotland. Scottish Journal of Geology 44(2), 151–168.
doc.comment: The principal focus is acritarchs. The whole supplied text, including captions and Figure 8, was read. The local PDF's embedded Figures 5–7 are clipped, preventing complete sample-level extraction; formation-level lists retain records whose sample assignments cannot be recovered. Formation summaries overlap the separately described samples below and must not be counted as independent collections. Figure 8 combines Henshaw data from this study and Wellman & Richardson (1993), Terrestrial plant microfossils from Silurian inliers of the Midland Valley of Scotland; Knockgardner data are from Dorning (1982), Early Wenlock acritarchs from the Knockgardner and Straiton Grit Formations of Knockgardner, Ayrshire. No spore specimens are illustrated.

items.locality: Pentland Hills inliers, Midland Valley of Scotland
items.section_or_core: North Esk, Bavelaw Castle and Loganlee inliers
items.age_basis_detail: Graptolite dating attributed to Bull & Loydell (1995); acritarch assemblages are consistent with this age.
items.notes: Formation-level occurrence list from Figure 8, labelled Pentland Hills. Acritarchs dominate; in productive North Esk samples they exceed 90% of the microflora. Cryptospores occur consistently in low numbers in the highest four North Esk samples, MPA 43843, 43296, 43847 and 43846. North Esk samples MPA 42011, 43849 and 43848 were barren. An alternative deep-water submarine-fan interpretation and possible palynomorph redistribution in turbidites are discussed, without a claim of stratigraphical reworking. This summary overlaps the separately listed Loganlee sample.

items.notes: Figure 8 gives a combined Pentland Hills formation list; occurrence assignments between the two inliers cannot be recovered from the clipped charts. Cryptospores are collectively rare. The lagoon interpretation includes fluctuating salinity culminating in brackish or freshwater conditions. The proposed stage range allows the explicitly discussed uncertainty in the position of the Llandovery–Wenlock boundary. Overlaps the separately described highest North Esk sample.

items.notes: Figure 8 explicitly combines records from Wellman & Richardson (1993) and this study, so the listed taxa cannot all be attributed independently to the new samples. Spores and cryptospores are more abundant and diverse than in the underlying formations; marine microfossils are few.
